description: This topic covers phrasal verbs (verb plus particle or preposition), their literal and idiomatic meanings, separable and inseparable forms, and common collocations including the correct prepositions used after particular verbs and adjectives.

options.text: A verb made up of a verb and one or more particles such as a preposition or adverb
A single verb that has more than three syllables
A noun that has been changed into a verb
A verb that is always written in the past tense

mcq.explanation: A phrasal verb combines a verb with a particle (a preposition or adverb), and the combination often has a meaning different from the verb alone, for example 'give up'.

mcq.questionText: Choose the meaning of the phrasal verb in: 'My grandmother is too weak to look after herself.'
mcq.explanation: 'Look after' means to take care of or be responsible for someone or something.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence uses 'give up' correctly to mean 'stop trying'?

options.text: She gave up smoking last year for the sake of her health.
Do not give up; you can still pass the examination if you study.
He gave up his seat to an elderly woman on the bus.
The soldiers gave up their weapons to the officer.

mcq.explanation: Here 'give up' means to stop trying or abandon an effort. The other sentences use 'give up' with different meanings such as stop a habit or surrender something.

mcq.questionText: Complete the collocation: 'The committee will _____ a decision tomorrow.'
mcq.explanation: The correct collocation is 'make a decision'. We do not say 'do a decision' or 'take a decision' in standard usage.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct preposition: 'My young brother is very good _____ mathematics.'
mcq.explanation: The adjective 'good' collocates with the preposition 'at' when talking about skills or abilities, as in 'good at mathematics'.

mcq.questionText: Which phrasal verb best replaces the underlined word? 'The car suddenly STOPPED WORKING on the highway.'
mcq.explanation: 'Break down' means to stop functioning, especially for a machine or vehicle. 'Break into' means to enter by force, 'break up' means to end a relationship, and 'break out' means to start suddenly.

mcq.questionText: What does 'put off' mean in: 'They decided to put off the meeting until next week.'?
mcq.explanation: 'Put off' means to postpone or delay something to a later time.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct sentence showing that 'turn down' is separable.

options.text: She turned down the offer because the salary was too low.
She turned the offer down because the salary was too low.
She turned down it because the salary was too low.
She down turned the offer because the salary was too low.

mcq.explanation: A separable phrasal verb allows the object (a noun) to come between the verb and particle, as in 'turned the offer down'. Note that with a pronoun the object must come between them ('turned it down'), so option C is wrong.

mcq.questionText: Which phrasal verb means 'to use all of a supply so that none is left'?
mcq.explanation: 'Run out of' means to have no more of something left, for example 'We have run out of fuel.'

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct preposition: 'Children should not depend _____ their parents forever.'
mcq.explanation: The verb 'depend' is always followed by the preposition 'on' (or 'upon') when it means to rely on someone or something.

mcq.questionText: In which sentence does 'carry out' carry its idiomatic meaning of 'perform' or 'complete'?

options.text: The workers will carry out the boxes to the lorry.
Please carry out the chairs from the hall.
The scientists will carry out an experiment on water purification.
He carried out his bag and left the room.

mcq.explanation: 'Carry out' idiomatically means to perform or complete a task such as an experiment or an order. The other sentences use the literal meaning of physically taking something outside.

mcq.questionText: Which option is the correct collocation for daily school routine?
mcq.explanation: The standard collocation is 'do homework'. Although a teacher may 'give homework', the act of completing it is 'do homework'.

mcq.questionText: What does the idiomatic phrasal verb 'come across' mean in: 'While cleaning, I came across an old photograph.'?
mcq.explanation: 'Come across' means to find or meet something or someone unexpectedly, by chance.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct preposition: 'She is deeply interested _____ studying medicine abroad.'
mcq.explanation: The adjective 'interested' is followed by the preposition 'in', as in 'interested in studying'.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence shows an INSEPARABLE phrasal verb used correctly?

options.text: We looked the problem after carefully.
We looked after the children all afternoon.
We looked the children after all afternoon.
We after looked the children all afternoon.

mcq.explanation: 'Look after' is inseparable, so the object cannot come between the verb and the particle. It must stay together as 'look after the children'.

fib.questionText: Many young people find it hard to give _____ bad habits such as smoking.
fib.explanation: 'Give up' means to stop doing something, especially a habit.

fib.questionText: The pilot was praised for his ability to carry _____ the difficult mission successfully.
fib.explanation: 'Carry out' means to perform or complete a task such as a mission or duty.

fib.questionText: We had to put _____ the wedding because of the heavy rain.
fib.explanation: 'Put off' means to postpone or delay an event.

fib.questionText: Our hardworking teacher is very good _____ explaining difficult topics.
fib.explanation: The adjective 'good' is followed by 'at' when referring to a skill or ability.

fib.questionText: The success of the project will depend _____ the support of the community.
fib.explanation: The verb 'depend' collocates with the preposition 'on' (or 'upon').

fib.questionText: After driving for hours, we suddenly ran out _____ petrol in the middle of nowhere.
fib.explanation: The phrasal verb is 'run out of', meaning to have none of a supply left.

fib.questionText: Please remember to make a _____ before you book the bus tickets.
fib.explanation: The correct collocation is 'make a decision'.

fib.questionText: While reading the old book, she came _____ a letter written by her great-grandfather.
fib.explanation: 'Come across' means to find something unexpectedly.

fib.questionText: He politely turned _____ the job offer because it was too far from home.
fib.explanation: 'Turn down' means to refuse or reject an offer.

fib.questionText: My elder sister has agreed to look _____ our baby while my mother is at work.
fib.explanation: 'Look after' means to take care of someone.

tf.questionText: A phrasal verb is formed by combining a verb with a particle such as a preposition or an adverb.
tf.explanation: By definition, a phrasal verb is a verb plus one or more particles.

tf.questionText: The phrasal verb 'give up' always keeps the literal meaning of physically handing something upward.
tf.explanation: Phrasal verbs are often idiomatic. 'Give up' usually means to stop trying or to quit, not a literal upward action.

tf.questionText: In the sentence 'Look after the baby', the phrasal verb 'look after' is inseparable.
tf.explanation: 'Look after' is inseparable, so the object cannot come between 'look' and 'after'.

tf.questionText: With a separable phrasal verb, when the object is a pronoun it must come between the verb and the particle.
tf.explanation: For example, we say 'turn it down', not 'turn down it'. The pronoun goes between the two parts.

tf.questionText: The expression 'good at' is the correct collocation for talking about a skill, while 'good in' is not standard.
tf.explanation: We say 'good at football' or 'good at English', using 'at' for skills.

tf.questionText: The phrase 'do a decision' is the correct collocation in standard English.
tf.explanation: The correct collocation is 'make a decision', not 'do a decision'.

tf.questionText: 'Break down' and 'break into' have the same meaning.
tf.explanation: 'Break down' means to stop functioning, while 'break into' means to enter by force. They are different.

tf.questionText: The verb 'depend' should be followed by the preposition 'on' rather than 'of'.
tf.explanation: The correct form is 'depend on' (or 'depend upon').

tf.questionText: 'Run out of' means to have plenty of a supply remaining.
tf.explanation: 'Run out of' means the opposite: to have used up all of a supply so that none is left.

tf.questionText: The phrasal verb 'put off' can be used to mean postpone, as in 'They put off the match because of rain.'
tf.explanation: 'Put off' commonly means to postpone or delay an event.

summary.questionText: Define a phrasal verb in one sentence.
summary.correctAnswer: A phrasal verb is a combination of a verb and one or more particles (a preposition or adverb) that often has a meaning different from the verb on its own.
summary.explanation: This captures both the structure (verb plus particle) and the idiomatic nature of phrasal verbs.

summary.questionText: Explain the difference between a literal and an idiomatic meaning of a phrasal verb, with an example.
summary.correctAnswer: A literal meaning is the plain combination of the words, while an idiomatic meaning is special and not predictable; for example, 'carry out the box' is literal, but 'carry out an experiment' is idiomatic, meaning to perform it.
summary.explanation: Many phrasal verbs have both meanings depending on context.

summary.questionText: What is the difference between a separable and an inseparable phrasal verb?
summary.correctAnswer: A separable phrasal verb allows the object to come between the verb and the particle (turn the offer down), while an inseparable phrasal verb must keep the verb and particle together (look after the child).
summary.explanation: Knowing this helps in placing objects correctly, especially pronouns.

summary.questionText: Give two correct verb-plus-noun collocations and the single verb that pairs with each.
summary.correctAnswer: Make a decision and do homework; 'make' pairs with decision and 'do' pairs with homework.
summary.explanation: Collocations are fixed word partnerships that must be learned together.

summary.correctAnswer: A collocation is a pair or group of words that are habitually used together and sound natural, such as 'make a decision' or 'good at sports'.
summary.explanation: Collocations are about natural word partnerships in English.

summary.questionText: Replace the underlined verb with a phrasal verb: 'The machine STOPPED FUNCTIONING during the test.'
summary.correctAnswer: The machine broke down during the test.
summary.explanation: 'Break down' is the phrasal verb that means to stop functioning.

summary.questionText: Replace the phrasal verb with a single verb of similar meaning: 'She decided to POSTPONE the journey.'
summary.correctAnswer: She decided to put off the journey (or: She decided to postpone the journey).
summary.explanation: 'Put off' is the phrasal verb equivalent of the single verb 'postpone'.

summary.questionText: Why is it important to use the correct preposition after certain verbs and adjectives? Give one example.
summary.correctAnswer: Using the correct preposition keeps the sentence grammatically correct and natural; for example, we must say 'interested in', not 'interested on'.
summary.explanation: Wrong prepositions make sentences sound unnatural and may change or confuse the meaning.

summary.questionText: List the correct prepositions that follow these words: good ___, interested ___, depend ___.
summary.correctAnswer: good at, interested in, depend on.
summary.explanation: These are fixed preposition collocations that must be memorised.

summary.questionText: Use the phrasal verb 'look after' in a complete sentence and state its meaning.
summary.correctAnswer: Example: 'I look after my younger brother after school.' It means to take care of someone.
summary.explanation: 'Look after' is an inseparable phrasal verb meaning to take care of.

hoq.questionText: Read the sentence: 'The headmaster refused to put up with the noise, so he turned down the request for an extra break and asked the prefects to carry out his orders.' Which list correctly gives the meanings of the three phrasal verbs in order?
hoq.explanation: 'Put up with' means to tolerate, 'turn down' means to reject, and 'carry out' means to perform. Only option B gives all three meanings correctly in order.

hoq.questionText: Choose the sentence that is correct in BOTH phrasal-verb separability AND preposition collocation.

options.text: She is good in music, so she turned the offer down and looked after her studies.
She is good at music, so she turned down the offer and looked her studies after.
She is good at music, so she turned the offer down and looked after her studies.
She is good on music, so she turned down it and looked after her studies.

hoq.explanation: The correct collocation is 'good at music'. 'Turn down' is separable, so 'turned the offer down' is valid, and 'look after' is inseparable, so 'looked after her studies' is correct. Option C satisfies all rules.

hoq.questionText: Which sentence correctly replaces a single verb with a suitable phrasal verb WITHOUT changing the meaning? Original: 'The factory will INVESTIGATE the cause of the accident and may CANCEL production.'

options.text: The factory will look into the cause of the accident and may call off production.
The factory will look after the cause of the accident and may put off production.
The factory will come across the cause of the accident and may turn down production.
The factory will run out of the cause of the accident and may break down production.

hoq.explanation: 'Look into' means to investigate and 'call off' means to cancel, so option A preserves the meaning. The other options use phrasal verbs with the wrong meanings.
